shots.text: Wrigley mailed free gum to a million strangers.
He didn't start in gum — he started in soap, giving away free baking powder with every bar.
Customers wanted the baking powder more than the soap.
So he dropped soap, and sold baking powder instead.
Then he gave away free gum with every order — and the same thing happened again.
They wanted the gum more than the baking powder.
So he dropped baking powder, and bet everything on gum.
In nineteen fifteen, he grabbed every phone book in America.
And mailed free gum to every single address inside.
One and a half million homes got gum nobody ordered.
His logic: if you could afford a phone, you could afford gum.
Four years later, he mailed it again — to seven million homes.
Today, Wrigley gum is sold in almost every country on Earth.
